rich:
dryxiogta, a modder made these portals between GTA III, GTA: Vice City and GTA: San Andreas

All three games run inside the same process, sharing one Direct3D device. Each portal is a live GPU texture, the other gam is actually running behind it (not a vid or a captured window) Walking through swaps which engine has control and the others keep running.

Each game keeps its own saves, missions and settings. Each world continues running it's own AI, traffic and physics in real time.

rich:
Collections

One of the most unique features ScholarXIV comes with are Collections; a shareable list of papers that any user on the platform can curate and make public.

Collections let you group related papers in an organized fashion. Then you can add or remove papers as your research evolves, keeping each collection focused around a topic, project, literature review, or area of interest.

You can also create shareable links for your collections and invite others as either editors or viewers. This makes it easy to collaborate without losing structure. If you want your collection to reach more people, you can set it public and it will appear in the Discover Collections feed.

The Discover Collections feed is where you can explore public collections created by other ScholarXIV users. It is a simple way to find high-quality paper lists, discover new research areas, and build your own library faster. From this feed you can add Collections to your own library.

Research is easier when papers are not scattered across tabs, folders, and disconnected tools. ScholarXIV Collections help you organize, share, collaborate, and discover papers in one place.

Sandboxes

ScholarXIV comes with a built-in Sandbox tool that lets your research agent run code, simulations, calculations, and more right inside your research workflow.

Sandboxes give your research agent computational advantages. Instead of relying only on next-token prediction, your agent can write and run code in the Sandbox to calculate results, test ideas, and give you more accurate answers.

Your research agent can also run simulations inside Sandboxes to help you conduct deeper research. This brings a whole new dimension to how you explore hypotheses, compare outcomes, and validate research-backed insights.

That's not all. You or your research agent can use the Sandbox to generate graphs, plot figures, create files, analyze data, and so much more. So you can go from running simulations to visualizing the results and exporting them, all in one place.

You don't have to switch between separate coding tools, notebooks, charting apps, and research assistants just to get computational work done. ScholarXIV brings research, reasoning, code execution, and visualization together in one seamless experience.
